text:
sara: Heads-up: ran a staging run of the Go sampleapp with aggressive batching + prefetch and saw a cascade of soft 429s and long tail streaming stalls. Reproable.

_dom: What config did you use?_

sara: Steps: 1) sdk.batch_window_ms=50 2) prefetch=2 3) run `wrk -c40 -t4 -d60s` against /v1/chat/stream. After ~30s soft 429s start appearing and queued grows.

sara: Logs:```
WARN quota: soft_429_rate=0.028 window_ms=50
INFO batch: window_ms=50 inflight=118 queued=360
WARN backpressure: lease_wait_timeout lease_id=lk_7 held_by=retry-path
```

lee: That pattern smells like synchronized prefetch + no jitter on retry/batch flush. If many clients flush exactly at batch_window boundary you can get bursty token-bucket drains.

dom: Is this Go-only? JS SDK had a jittered prefetch flush we added last quarter.

sara: Confirmed: JS staging didn't show the same tail. Go SDK code uses `time.Sleep(batchWindow)` without randomization; JS used `setTimeout(rand(0,batchWindow))`.

omar: Two related issues then: 1) lack of jitter -> synchronized bursts, 2) prefetch spawn reserves quota before validating cursor -> double-reserve on retries. Combined they blow out the token bucket quickly.

sara: I prototyped a small change: move reserve into the worker after cursor validation and add jitter on spawn: `sleep(rand.Intn(batchWindowMs))`. Quick staging run cut soft_429_rate from ~2.8% to ~0.3%.

dom: Nice. Can you open a tiny PR for SDK-go? We should also add a unit test that simulates N clients flush-aligned and assert no >1.0% soft_429_rate.

sara: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/321 (WIP) - "fix: prefetch jitter + defer reserve until validated". Includes a bench test.

omar: Plan from my side: 1) add explicit jitter parameter to Go SDK defaults (jitter_enabled=true, jitter_max_ms=batch_window_ms), 2) add per-tenant token-bucket caps to avoid cross-tenant starvation, 3) add telemetry: `soft_429_rate`, `prefetch_jitter_applied`, `prefetch_double_reserve`.

lee: We should also add an adaptive window heuristic: if queue growth > X% over 30s, increase batch_window_ms by factor 1.5 up to a cap. That smooths bursts without manual tuning.

dom: Agree, but adaptive heuristics need canarying. For now let's ship jitter + deferred reserve as hotfix. Then iterate with adaptive windows.

devex-bot: Issue created: #5510-prefetch-burst-jitter (assigned to omar) - https://issues.redwood.ai/5510

omar: Canary plan: deploy sdk-go with jitter to staging, run sweep tests with batch_window_ms in [20,50,100] and prefetch=1..3. Abort if `soft_429_rate` > 1% for 5m. I'll also monitor `permits_held_ms` p90.

sara: I'll update the sampleapp README and add a short note in devex: "Go SDK: prefer jitter_enabled=true and consider batch_window_ms=75ms for medium QPS streaming workloads."

lee: Add a short snippet to onboarding docs explaining why jitter matters for client-side batching and prefetch. Also call out how to toggle per-tenant caps.

sara: Will include the doc blurb in the PR. Linking logs and perf outputs in the issue.

dom: Thanks team. Good catch before it hit prod. :thumbsup:
